candidates.title: Sporting Look, evening fashions
candidates.creator: Toni Frissell
candidates.rights: Free to Use and Reuse / Library of Congress curated set
candidates.caption: The image is a distinct authored work around fashion; the clothes, staging, model, commission, publication, and photograph do not collapse into one ownership question.
candidates.alt: Two models wearing evening fashions in a 1956 Toni Frissell photograph made for Sports Illustrated.
candidates.credit: Toni Frissell Collection, Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division
candidates.relevance: Material witness installed in the related exhibitions.

candidates.caption: The sheet demonstrates a contract-shaped network of design, printing, manufacture, advertising, attribution, and distribution—even when the operative agreements are absent from the image.

candidates.title: Evening dress

candidates.caption: The record separates the material dress, House of Worth attribution, Charles Frederick Worth design credit, accession, and the museum’s present custody.

candidates.creator: House of Worth; attributed to Charles Frederick Worth and Jean-Philippe Worth
candidates.rights: Public Domain / Met Open Access
candidates.caption: The dual designer attribution makes succession visible as an evidence question: house continuity does not erase uncertainty about individual authorship.
candidates.alt: Ornate pale silk House of Worth ball gown with floral decoration and a full trained skirt, dated 1895 to 1900.

candidates.title: Fancy dress costume
candidates.creator: House of Worth
candidates.rights: Public Domain / Met Open Access
candidates.caption: An accession-quality record preserves a house object beyond the founder’s lifetime while keeping the object, maker attribution, and museum stewardship distinct.
candidates.alt: Elaborate House of Worth silk fancy dress costume with a fitted bodice, dark patterned skirt, and dramatic decorative sleeves, around 1893.
candidates.credit: Gift of James A. and Mary Elizabeth Kingsland, 1994
candidates.relevance: Material witness installed in the related exhibitions.

candidates.title: Evening dress
candidates.creator: House of Worth
candidates.rights: Public Domain / Met Open Access
candidates.caption: Made after Charles Frederick Worth’s death, the dress lets the house name continue in the record without proving who controlled every creative or economic decision.
candidates.alt: House of Worth silk evening dress from 1898 to 1900 with a pale embellished bodice, narrow waist, and richly patterned trained skirt.
candidates.credit: Gift of Miss Eva Drexel Dahlgren, 1976
candidates.relevance: Material witness installed in the related exhibitions.

candidates.title: Gloria Vanderbilt Cooper
candidates.creator: Toni Frissell
candidates.rights: Free to Use and Reuse / Library of Congress curated set
candidates.caption: The frame is not neutral delivery: pose, setting, crop, light, garment, commission, and publication context combine to manufacture a public fashion meaning.
candidates.alt: Gloria Vanderbilt Cooper photographed by Toni Frissell for Vogue in 1966.
candidates.credit: Toni Frissell Collection, Library of Congress Prints and Photographs Division
candidates.relevance: Material witness installed in the related exhibitions.

candidates.title: Ball gown
candidates.creator: House of Worth
candidates.rights: Public Domain / Met Open Access
candidates.caption: Materials such as silk, glass, and metallic thread make skilled transformation visible while the museum record still names only the house as maker.
candidates.alt: House of Worth ball gown from about 1887, with a structured pale silk silhouette and elaborate surface ornament.
candidates.relevance: Material witness installed in the related exhibitions.

candidates.title: Walking suit
candidates.creator: House of Worth
candidates.rights: Public Domain / Met Open Access
candidates.caption: A finished suit can preserve the house name while leaving the cutters, fitters, stitchers, finishers, and production negotiations unnamed.
candidates.alt: Dark silk House of Worth walking suit from about 1889, photographed frontally against a neutral background.
candidates.credit: Brooklyn Museum Costume Collection at The Metropolitan Museum of Art; Gift of the Princess Viggo in accordance with the wishes of the Misses Hewitt, 1931
candidates.relevance: Material witness installed in the related exhibitions.

candidates.title: Ensemble
candidates.creator: House of Worth
candidates.rights: Public Domain / Met Open Access
candidates.caption: The ensemble carries material decisions across components; the surviving object cannot narrate every demonstration, correction, and embodied judgment that produced them.
candidates.alt: House of Worth ensemble from 1893 in dark silk with jet and metal ornament, shown frontally.
candidates.credit: Brooklyn Museum Costume Collection at The Metropolitan Museum of Art; Gift of Edith Gardiner, 1926
